We have just received this list, and at present, we simply cannot say whether all the persons indicated in these death certificates are indeed dead, and we should like to take the liberty to, after verifying the individual persons or not, and we should therefore like to be allowed to state whether we object or do not object to individual death certificates only after verifying whether indeed that such and such a person is dead and has been confirmed as dead. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that there are two different elements in what Counsel Radovic has just said. I think he is questioning the procedure followed by the Vitez authorities and through which the death certificates were issued. I don't know if Counsel Radovic is contesting the authenticity itself of the document, that is, the signature and the authority which issued the documents, and I think that it's only if Mr. Radovic is contesting the authenticity of the document and the authority that issued the documents, then I think we should have a discussion. But if Mr. Radovic is contesting something else, then I don't think it should prevent us from tendering these documents into evidence, and I think I have understood what Mr. Radovic said rightly. But these documents, these 93 death certificates, can be admitted into evidence, and we will wait for Mr. Radovic to prove that the persons that were officially dead or reported as dead are, in fact, alive, which would be very good news.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Counsel Slokovic-Glumac?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Your Honours, just one thing. A very casual glance at this text, because this has not been classified properly, put in order, but we see that there is a death certificate for one Ibrahim Karic and it is among these death certificates, and here the witness we heard today said that Ibrahim Karic was alive and that his name appeared on the list of dead persons by mistake. So it seems that this documentation has also not been really put into proper order or, rather, brought into agreement with testimony of witnesses. Ibrahim Karic, number 68, is alive, as the witness testified today. So I think one really has to go through this list to see whose are these death certificates. Sixty-eight, the witness who was additionally examined today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Sorry. Did you say it's number 68, Ibrahim Karic?

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: Quite right, Ibrahim Karic. This list from the notes of the witness that we checked against the HVO list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. Is he on the --

utterances.speaker: MS. SLOKOVIC-GLUMAC
utterances.text: His death certificate is here, 00496900, he is again -- that is on this list, so this list of death certificates is not accurate either, but we need to go through it and then give you our final view on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: Mr. President, once more, as far as this case in particular, the case of Ibrahim Karic, if I remember well, the witness this morning or yesterday, I'm not sure -- maybe we can check the transcript -- the witness said that he had suppressed this name on his notes because someone told him that he was alive. That's all. It seems that there is a contradiction between this hypothetical statement and an official statement issued by an official authority saying officially, and in conformity with the legal procedures in this country at that time, showing that there was a death. But if the quality and the identity of the authority which issued this document is not contested, then we can tender this document. Of course, maybe this list should be compared at a later stage with other lists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. We believe the Prosecutor is right. These documents, the death certificates, can be admitted into evidence subject, of course, to any challenge from the Defence when the Defence starts with its case, and then they can produce evidence to the effect that the particular death certificate is not accurate. Yes, Counsel Pavkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAVKOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, yesterday, when we were discussing the list which was explained to us by the witness, I objected then because under 18, in that list and here on this list, under 82, there it was NN and then somebody, whom we have failed to identify, had added by hand Muzafer Puscul. Now, in this list, under 82, we see that it says Muzafer Puscul who was killed on the 16th of April, 1993. I therefore second the proposal of my colleagues to go through this more carefully, more carefully, but now, because one can never be prudent enough, not to admit it as evidence because it has not been established beyond doubt that that person, that is the anonymous person under 18, was indeed Muzafer Puscul.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We are at cross-purposes because yesterday it was a different problem, whether the body of a particular person buried there was the body of Muzafer Puscul. The question now is whether Muzafer Puscul is dead, and we have an official certificate of the relevant competent authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina stating that he is dead. We have already ruled on this matter. This will be admitted into evidence subject to any challenge by the Defence; whenever you can prove that actually he is not dead, he is alive. As long as you can prove that Mr. Muzafer Puscul is alive, fine. It's not a question of whether his body is there; whether or not he's dead. This is what this set of documents is designed to certify, that those people are dead. All right. Any other document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The second document, Mr. President, will not be contested. You will remember that during the testimony of Witness II (sic), there was a statement which was not signed and which was handed by the Prosecution to the Defence counsel. You wished that an affidavit taken from the investigator of the Tribunal be handed to the Defence counsel. That's what I'm doing now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 328.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: I would like to make a correction. It's Witness EE, EE in English. The third document I would like to hand to the Tribunal is this one. On various occasions, you had to deal with the case related to the suitcase, the briefcase that Vlatko Kupreskic had when he was arrested and which contained a certain number of documents. We kept one of those documents -- actually, a photocopy of it -- and we would like to tender this document. We have the original of this document. It is an official document certifying that from the 16th February, 1993, Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic was a member of the HVO forces. You have the original here. I can add to this document an affidavit of the investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor who went through the whole documents contained in the briefcase, and he is saying in this document that the document we are now submitting was indeed in Mr. Vlatko Kupreskic's briefcase. Attached to the original we add a translation into English.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 329. The English translation 329A.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: The fourth document, Mr. President, will not be contested either. Before your visit to Bosnia next week, you wished to have certain data, demographic information, ethnic, economic and, if possible, social data regarding the various ethnic groups in Bosnia. We don't have a lot of information, but we would like to submit the following document to you. It's the figures from the 1991 census, and you will see that there is a corresponding map with different colours showing the distribution of various ethnic groups in this area of Central Bosnia. I would like to have more information to submit; however, we don't have this kind of information, apart from maybe the documents from Mrs. Bringa which are not part of the evidence but have been tendered into evidence pending a decision from the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 330.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: We have one last document to submit, but I leave it to Mr. Moskowitz to speak about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Mr. President, there is one other document that we have. It was, in fact, filed on September 11th, 1998, pursuant to Rule 94 bis, testimony of expert witness, and it was filed and provided, copies provided to Defence counsel to determine whether or not Defence counsel would accept this information and not require an expert witness to be called. I do not believe that we have received a response from Defence counsel one way or the other regarding this exhibit, and we therefore wish to tender it now and assume that Defence counsel does not object to it. It is simply a report that lists the level of destruction of properties in the Lasva Valley, and particularly mentions Ahmici and the number of houses that were destroyed in Ahmici. The report was produced by the International Management Group which conducted this investigation, I believe in 1975 (sic), for UNHCR in order to make an assessment of the damage in the valley and then to make a recommendation about the cost for repair. In fact, when the Tribunal goes to Ahmici next week, I think you will see that there has been a good deal of repair going on in Ahmici even now. We have attached to this report the statement of the expert witness that we would have called, Mediha Mlaco, who participated as a civil engineer in the survey and specifically went into Ahmici and helped in compiling the statistics for that particular village which can be found on page 38 of the IMF report under the heading of "Vitez," and under that heading of "Vitez" there is the village of Ahmici, and then next to the village of Ahmici, a series of columns listing the kinds of damage noted by this particular witness. So we would offer this evidence to the Tribunal because we feel it is useful for the Tribunal in determining the level of destruction in the village and goes particularly, we think, to Count 1, the persecution count.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 331.

utterances.speaker: MR. TERRIER
utterances.text: We are finished, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Exhibit 331.
